title: The Mercury Theatre on the Air
paragraphs: Only 18 objects belong to Mercury Theatre on the Air proper; later items are separately profiled by historical program.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] (performer, host, and radio adaptor), Bernard Herrmann (conductor, composer, and music), Ray Collins (performer and narrator), Dan Seymour (announcer and performer), Edgar Barrier (performer), George Coulouris (performer), and Eustace Wyatt (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.b1c76a6702c1bee9|WABC]], [[org|org.f8fbca558a370a00|WBT]], and [[org|org.9cc47908c68e2d15|WRVA]].
The stories often return to literary adaptation, war and military service, horror and supernatural, and aviation.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Mercury Theatre on the Air launch, War of the Worlds broadcast, Campbell Playhouse transition, and Ceiling Unlimited wartime aviation series.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|the-shadow|The Shadow]], [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], [[show|suspense|Suspense]], and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]].
